newsitem.title: ITALY: Mercedes Italy against car incentive plans.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes Italy against car incentive plans.

text.p: The chairman of Mercedes Benz Italia, part of Daimler Benz AG, Jochen Prange said he was against car buying incentives to boost vehicle markets since they disrupt the market in successive years.
Speaking about car incentive schemes in Italy, Prange said that he did not believe that the Italian government had enough money for a car buying scheme.
"I do not believe in incentives because they do not create new clients...I believe it has a disastrous effect on the following year," he told reporters.

Prange was meeting with reporters to talk about its new Class A model which Mercedes plans to launches in autumn 1997. Mercedes hopes to sell some 15,000 Class A models per year in Italy at a price of between 30 million and 35 million lire.
The Class A will be available in two petrol engine versions and a diesel engine.
With sales of Class A, Mercedes hopes to reach 60,600 unit sales in Italy during 1998, from an estimated 37,100 in 1996 and a forecast 47,000 in 1997, said Prange.

On Sunday, Italy's prime minister Romano Prodi said he did not believe special financial incentives were the best way to revive falling car sales in Italy. He said an incentive scheme could boost sales temporarily but there would be a slump after the measures were phased out.
